nature: Independent AI verification; not a human audit, not a user test, not evidence of user effect.

findings.area: Tiers / stripe-texture comfort bound (row 21), sections 2.2 item 4, 3.4 and 13; matrix row 21 prototype cell
findings.problem: The texts contradict each other about what 'inside' and 'outside' the bound mean. Section 2.2 says a texture with more than five light-dark pairs above 1.5:1 'is outside it' (a violation). Section 3.4, section 13 and the row 21 prototype cell say the reduced-motion progress stripes (17.4:1 to 21:1, more than five pairs on tracks wider than 80 px) 'fall inside the bound', which reads as compliance. The stripes in fact break the bound. Section 13 still says 'replace it', so the required action is clear, but a reader could take the stripes as compliant. The tier itself is acceptable: the rule has an access reason (pattern discomfort in people with migraine, PER-WILKINS84) and only constrains artwork after calibration.
findings.fix: Replace 'fall inside the bound' with 'are within the scope of the bound and break it' in section 3.4, section 13 and the matrix row 21 prototype cell.

findings.area: Evidence grading, row 53 (reminders after acquired brain injury, strong)
findings.problem: Strong rests on two sources. COG-GILL11 is a descriptive systematic review of 91 studies across mixed clinical populations, with no pooled effect and no quality appraisal reported in its abstract. COG-WILS01 is one randomised crossover trial (n = 143), re-resolved here. The fixed scale's letter ('systematic review') allows strong. In substance the target-population evidence is one well-controlled RCT plus a review whose population only partly matches. Synthesis rule 3 (another population caps the grade at limited) is not explicitly reconciled with the mixed population of GILL11.
findings.fix: Either lower the core part to moderate, or add one sentence to the section 1.4 table and the row 53 caveat. It should say why rule 3 does not cap the mixed-population review, and that GILL11 does not appraise study quality.

findings.area: Evidence grading, section 4 'Colour-blind correcting glasses' (contradicted, PER-GOMEZ18 sole source)
findings.problem: Rule 6 requires a study that is 'not small'. The abstract gives no sample size, only 'a high number of individuals'. PER-PIEPENBROCK13 was moved from contradicted to insufficient for the same missing sample size, so the two cases are treated differently. The difference is defensible, because only the GOMEZ18 abstract asserts a large sample. Optics Express is open access, but the publisher fetch in this verification hit a bot challenge (HTTP 202, 598 bytes), so the sample size was not established here either.
findings.fix: Read the open-access full text and record n in section 4. If n cannot be established, apply the PIEPENBROCK13 treatment: insufficient, with the GOMEZ18 result as limited context.

findings.problem: Demoting a non-safety baseline row (row 62, full keyboard operation with no trap, a mandatory access limit in section 6.1) to 'setting' with a consistent axis edit makes check.py exit 0. The scratch mutation run confirmed this. The checker documents it as a known limit, but none of the mandatory access limits (no keyboard trap, never sound-only, speech never the only input, no data loss on time-out) is pinned.
findings.fix: Add a MANDATORY_BASELINE_TOPICS map like SAFETY_TOPICS: stable Adaptation regexes that must each match a baseline row. Extend the self-test to demote each of those rows with a consistent axis edit.

findings.problem: The value-set header says the Empirical evidence column grades the effect of the row's adaptation. In row 39 the grade 'contradicted' rates the dyslexia-font claim that the row rejects, not the adaptation itself (no dyslexia font as an aid; a plain reading-face preference later). Only the Verification cell explains this, so the column has two meanings.
findings.fix: State this exception in the value-set paragraph, or regrade the row's own adaptation and carry the contradicted dyslexia-font claim in section 4 only.

findings.problem: Row 24 cites ITU-R BT.1702-3 Guideline 1. Guideline 1 also warns that a flashing sequence lasting more than five seconds may be a risk even when it meets the thresholds. That clause is not reflected in the flash limit.
findings.fix: Add to row 24 that no system-drawn flashing sequence, even one under the thresholds, lasts more than 5 s, or record why that clause is not applied.

findings.problem: The bullet 'Observational reductions in incidence after broadcast guidelines' has no source id, although it is listed as empirical support for a safety limit.
findings.fix: Cite the source that reports the reductions, or mark the bullet as own inference or remove it.

findings.area: Tiers: row 26 / section 3.5 Q6 per-item reveal for third-party flashing media
findings.problem: The warned, non-persistent reveal is an exception carved out of a Q6 safety limit. The owner asked for limits that hold regardless of the chosen settings. The document keeps the reveal outside the guarantee, off, and gated on a clinical safety review, so nothing currently depends on a setting. Clinical approval alone is not an owner decision, however.
findings.fix: Record that offering the reveal also needs an explicit project-owner decision, in addition to the clinical safety review.

findings.area: Citation, INT-JACOB1991 on safety row 69 (and row 68)
findings.problem: INT-JACOB1991 resolves: title, year 1991 and ACM TOIS match by DOI in OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar. Neither index has a usable abstract, so the row 69 premise that unintended gaze activation is a known risk cannot be checked at abstract level. It is the only peer-reviewed source on safety row 69. No grade depends on it: row 69 is insufficient and rests on WCAG SC 3.2.1 and 2.5.2 plus a design rule.
findings.fix: Mark the source resolution as 'resolved (metadata only; claim from full text not read)', or add a source whose abstract states the problem of unintended gaze activation.

findings.area: Design ambition (reasoned AI opinion), section 3.6 Q6 vestibular category exclusions
findings.problem: The baseline excludes whole-screen fly-through and zoom-through transitions by category. That exclusion rests on own design rules, and the vestibular evidence comes from other contexts, so it is graded at most limited. Section 12 priority 3 calibrates the area and duration bounds, but it does not say whether the category exclusion can be relaxed if the tests allow it. That leaves a class of spatial, futuristic transitions closed off without a calibration path.
findings.fix: Extend section 12 priority 3 to test bounded large-field zoom transitions (≤ 320 ms, once) with vestibular participants. State that the category exclusion is revisited on that result.

tiers_and_axes:
**Safety.** Never depends on a manual setting. All 11 'Safety:' rows are baseline, and check.py enforces that. The vestibular limit covers boot and first-run before any preference exists. The third-party flash guard is future research but is never a setting. The per-item reveal is outside the guarantee and not offered (minor: it needs an owner decision).

**Device preferences.** Followed automatically where the platform offers them:
- prefers-reduced-motion selects 'reduced';
- prefers-color-scheme, prefers-contrast or forced-colors, prefers-reduced-transparency, and the device text-size, caption and do-not-disturb states start their axes;
- natively, the profile store acts as the device preference (a profiles extension).

**Default not dulled.** The regular default is not made duller without a baseline reason. Stimulus 'regular' is the middle step, and 'rich' only adds. The vestibular limit restricts movement of surfaces larger than about a quarter of the display (once, ≤ 320 ms) and keeps light, opacity and glow free. The ask halo settles after 5 s on SC 2.2.2 (A) grounds. The stripe-texture comfort rule (row 21) is untagged baseline with an access reason (pattern discomfort, PER-WILKINS84) and constrains artwork only after calibration. The vestibular baseline is an explicit own tiering decision under the owner's 'dangerous visual effects without configuration' rule; that is acceptable, with bounds flagged for user test.

**Axes, rules and reset.**
- Axes are combinable properties (28 axes, one owner per rendered property).
- There are no diagnosis profiles, and presets are named combinations only.
- Combination rules: section 7.2 (one owner per property, fixed colour pipeline with floors re-verified, preferences as inputs, presets).
- Conflict resolution: section 5, 13 conflicts.
- Findability and reset: section 7.3 (settings, quick tile, trusted screens, first-run, per-axis reset and an undoable reset-all; safety rows are not resettable).

design_ambition:
Reasoned AI opinion, not evidence of user effect.

The proposal supports a light, futuristic, refined default and treats settings as variants of the same identity:
- Section 6.1 states that no baseline item dulls the default.
- Section 6.2 and the axis table keep materials, place colours, Orbit, typography and the light-blade language recognisable in every combination.
- 'rich' only adds intensity, and every flagship feature stays in the regular default.
- Polarity variants are both full-identity variants.
- The vestibular limit leaves light, glow and colour changes free and keeps the 1400 ms boot as a convergence of light.

Innovative principles are labelled in section 11 with the required tiers:
- **works now:** light-blade focus language, the static ask ring;
- **technically feasible:** invisible pointer assistance, ability-based calibration, the single input-timing axis, paired spacing, three-form numbers, the adaptive layer outside the familiar path;
- **future research:** semantic group scanning with gaze, the compositor flash guard, the on-device 'where was I' summary, the personal voice model.

One actionable shortfall (minor): the category exclusion of whole-screen zoom-through and fly-through transitions rests on own rules, and section 12 has no calibration path to relax it. Product default polarity is deferred to UX-A11Y-DS, which is acceptable.
limitations:
**Matrix reading.** The long Barrier, Adaptation, Normative-basis and Verification cells of all 92 rows were not read word by word. For every row I read Need, Tier, Axis, Grade, Sources, Prototype status, Native status and User test via a parsed dump. I read in full the 11 safety rows (Adaptation and Normative) and the rows graded strong, moderate or contradicted (Adaptation and Verification). SC and EN tokens were checked by regex over both whole files. The research text was read in full in slices.

**References not re-resolved.**
- Earlier-list references other than the required ones: COG-KUSTER17, COG-WERY16, PER-PIEPENBROCK13, INT-WOBBROCK2009, COG-ZORZI12 and others.
- About 50 further peer-reviewed references were not sampled.
- PER-GOMEZ18's sample size could not be established: the open-access full-text fetch hit a bot challenge.
- INT-JACOB1991 has no indexed abstract.
- Paywalled ISO and IEEE texts were not read.
- Platform documentation sources and W3C notes (COGA, low vision, NAUR, Core-AAM, MQ5) were not re-fetched.

**Not checked.**
- Native status reflects contract documents and code reads, not running code.
- The prototype was checked by grep and line reads, not rendered.
- No contrast, flash or reflow measurement was repeated.
- The harmonisation status of EN 301 549 V4.1.1 under the European Accessibility Act was not checked.

**Tools and inputs.**
- The hosted Graphify MCP was not used; code references were verified by literal reads.
- The exact required matrix column specification was not provided to this verifier, so the columns were judged against the owner's list.

**Nature of this review.** It is AI review only and is not evidence of user effect or a human accessibility audit. No user test exists for any row.
